findings.title: SEP-6/24/31 payment routing ignores the payer, so any account can credit another user's pending transaction using its memo
Payment asset identity is never enforced before SEP-6/24/31 funds-received notification
A non-AnchorException from SEP-31 handling falls through to SEP-24/SEP-6 matching for the same payment
Ledger transaction and operation used for crediting are taken from the same RPC that supplied the event, with no hash or event-to-operation binding
Soroban event filter does not bind to SAC contract IDs, so any contract that emits a matching transfer event is fetched and processed
SAC asset cache trusts the RPC entry without checking that it is for the requested contract
Soroban observer restart fails and stops detection
validate() dereferences a null asset when a non-SAC contract emits a transfer event
SAC metadata lookup indexes an empty RPC result without a check, throwing an unhandled exception
Horizon cursor restart jumps 200 operations forward, silently skipping network payments after downtime
Soroban RPC observer drops events that fail processing while still advancing the cursor
Horizon stream restart throws NumberFormatException on a transient Horizon failure and kills the status watcher
Failed SEP-24 handling falls through to SEP-6 matching on the same memo and account
Horizon observer advances its cursor past a payment whose dispatch failed, so the payment is never notified
Soroban observer's status field shadows the parent's status, so check() always reports GREEN after errors
Event-vs-ledger asset/amount cross-check cannot fire on the Soroban path, so the guard gives no independent protection
Outbound transfers from observed accounts are dispatched as received payments
Horizon invoke-contract branch reads only the first asset balance change, so transfers in later balance changes are missed
Amount/asset cross-check described as independent compares two values read from the same ledger operation on the Soroban path
Horizon events arriving before the observer is marked RUNNING are dropped, and the cursor then advances past them
Non-SAC lookups are not cached, so each transfer-shaped event from any contract costs one Soroban RPC call
Empty asset balance-change list on a transfer invoke crashes the Horizon stream handler and shuts the observer down
Silence-restart counter is never reset, so an observer that recovers is eventually shut down
restartInternal catches only TransactionException, so any other failure kills the status watcher
Soroban RPC observer cannot restart: executor is shut down in shutdownInternal, so restartInternal throws and the status watcher stops
In-memory RPC cursor advances before the database write, so a failed save diverges from the stored cursor
